_changes: 2026-11-15: dust_regolith, biology_sterility and caves_subsurface were briefly removed and then restored: they compare Earth sites with known lunar constants (Apollo regolith, sterile Moon) or a known Moon feature (the Tranquillitatis pit), which are valid analog tests even though they are the same for every Moon target.
_readme: Inference rule table. For a (Moon location, Earth location) pair and each experiment: check moon_precondition, compare category scores (config/categories.json, range -1..1) with the minimums, emit sufficient / partial / avoid / not_applicable, and attach 'also account for' caveats. Expressions use the same helpers as categories.json and are evaluated on the Moon row (moon_precondition) or Earth row (earth_hint).

decision_rule.not_applicable: moon_precondition is false (e.g. no ice at this Moon location), or a required category score is NaN
decision_rule.sufficient: every required category score >= its minimum
decision_rule.partial: otherwise: no required category below avoid_below, but at least one below its minimum. Report which required categories pass (those sub-tests are valid) and which do not
decision_rule.supporting: supporting categories never block; a supporting score below its value adds the note 'weak on <category>'
decision_rule.always_attach: experiment.also_account_for + mandatory_caveats of every required category + the global conditions listed in always_include

global_non_reproducible.consequence: traction, sinkage, plume ejecta ballistics, excavation reaction forces, structural loads, human gait and EVA workload all differ
global_non_reproducible.cover_with: gravity-offload rigs, mass-scaled rovers, parabolic flights, simulation

global_non_reproducible.earth_best: ~60-65 kPa at the highest analog sites (e.g. Dome C at 3,233 m)
global_non_reproducible.consequence: no convective cooling, ice sublimates instead of melting, outgassing, cold welding, electrostatic dust, no wind; LIBS and other instruments behave differently
global_non_reproducible.cover_with: thermal-vacuum (TVAC) and dirty-vacuum chambers with regolith simulant

global_non_reproducible.moon: galactic cosmic rays + solar particle events; ~1.4 mSv/day dose equivalent measured by Chang'e-4 (~200x Earth surface background)
global_non_reproducible.earth_best: atmosphere and magnetosphere shield every Earth site
global_non_reproducible.consequence: electronics single-event effects, materials ageing, crew dose limits

global_non_reproducible.earth_best: ~180-190 K surface minimum on the East Antarctic plateau
global_non_reproducible.consequence: material embrittlement, lubricant and battery failure, cryogenic ice strength, volatile trapping
global_non_reproducible.cover_with: cryo-vacuum chambers, LN2 (77 K) cold plates

global_non_reproducible.moon: sun within ~1.5 deg of the horizon plus topography; black shadows with no skylight
global_non_reproducible.earth_best: atmospheric scattering fills shadows; sun never that low for long except near the poles
global_non_reproducible.consequence: vision, navigation and solar-power results do not transfer
global_non_reproducible.cover_with: night tests with low-angle artificial light; ray-traced lunar illumination (LOLA)

global_non_reproducible.moon: agglutinates, glass, nanophase iron, sharp angular grains, very compact below ~30 cm
global_non_reproducible.earth_best: chemically weathered, rounded, moist soils with organics
global_non_reproducible.cover_with: certified simulants (e.g. LHS-1 / NU-LHT highland, LMS-1 / JSC-1A mare, GRC-3 geotechnical)

global_non_reproducible.moon: UV photoemission and solar-wind plasma charge the surface
global_non_reproducible.consequence: dust adhesion and levitation behave differently
contamination blanks and life-detection false positives

global_non_reproducible.moon: ~1.3 s one-way light time; no direct-to-Earth line of sight behind south-pole terrain
global_non_reproducible.cover_with: simulated latency and blackout windows in analog ops

experiments.name: Landing hazard detection & terrain-relative navigation
also_account_for: Lander-scale hazards (boulders, small craters) are below the 500 m slope baseline; verify with metre-scale DEMs.
Plume-surface interaction in vacuum (high-speed ejecta, no drag) cannot be reproduced outdoors on Earth.
Optical and lidar hazard detection must be tested under low-sun, no-skylight lighting (night tests with artificial light).
Vegetation, buildings and DSM artefacts can create false hazards on Earth.

experiments.name: Rover mobility & navigation
also_account_for: 1/6 g lowers wheel normal load: traction and sinkage change non-linearly; add mass-scaled or offloaded tests on a geotechnical simulant (e.g. GRC-3).
Moist, vegetated or rounded-grain Earth soils differ from dry, angular, compact lunar regolith.
No GNSS on the Moon: switch GPS off and navigate visually or by terrain-relative methods.
Low sun and black shadows degrade stereo vision; ~1.3 s latency and line-of-sight loss at the pole.

experiments.name: Ice prospecting (GPR, neutron spectrometer, drill-based detection)
also_account_for: Ice at 250-273 K (Earth) vs 25-110 K (Moon) changes GPR velocity/attenuation and drill response.
Earth's atmosphere blocks the cosmic-ray neutron source used for passive lunar neutron spectroscopy; Earth field tests need an active neutron source.
Earth permafrost contains liquid films, salts and organics; lunar ice carries other volatiles (CO, CO2, NH3, H2S, CH3OH).
Lunar ice distribution is set by sublimation in vacuum, not by climate or hydrology.

experiments.name: ISRU: excavation and extraction of icy regolith
also_account_for: In vacuum ice sublimates instead of melting: heating and vapour capture must be validated in a thermal-vacuum chamber.
Ice-cemented regolith at cryogenic temperature is much harder than Earth permafrost near 0 C.
Volatile contaminants (H2S, NH3, CO2 ...) need handling.
PSR operations: no sunlight for power, extreme cold soak.

experiments.name: Regolith excavation, berms, landing pads, sintering
also_account_for: 1/6 g reduces excavator weight and reaction force; lunar regolith is very compact below ~30 cm with interlocking angular grains.
Sintering and microwave heating depend on glass and nanophase iron absent from Earth tephra.
No water for concrete; binders outgas in vacuum.

experiments.name: Thermal control & power survival (extreme cold, long shadow/night)
also_account_for: No convection in vacuum: radiative loss dominates; Earth wind chill is the wrong heat-transfer mode.
PSR 25-110 K and long cold soaks cannot be reached outdoors (Earth minimum ~180 K): qualify in cryo-TVAC.
Earth polar night is seasonal and comes with an atmosphere; lunar shadow periods are set by topography.

experiments.name: Illumination & solar-power planning, low-sun-angle vision
also_account_for: Lunar south-pole sun stays within ~1.5 deg of the horizon; use LOLA illumination maps for numbers and Earth sites for procedures only.
No atmospheric scattering on the Moon: shadows are black.
Clouds and weather cut Earth solar input; the Moon has none.

experiments.name: Habitat, human operations, crew isolation
also_account_for: Isolation/remoteness is not scored by any category: prefer sites tagged 'isolation' (e.g. Concordia, HMP, MDRS).
No Earth site forces suited EVA and airlock cycles.
Lunar surface radiation ~1.4 mSv/day; ~3-day return to Earth; ~2.6 s round-trip comms.

experiments.name: Dust mitigation (seals, coatings, filters, suits)
also_account_for: Lunar dust is charged and moved by plume ejecta and electrostatics, not wind; Earth dust is wind-driven and moist.
Sharp glassy agglutinates are more abrasive than weathered Earth dust.
Verify seals and mechanisms in dirty-vacuum chambers with simulant.

experiments.name: Instrument field tests: spectrometers / mineralogy (VNIR, Raman, LIBS, XRF)
also_account_for: No space weathering on Earth (no nanophase-iron darkening and reddening).
Terrestrial anorthosite is more sodic than lunar ferroan anorthosite.
Atmospheric water bands (VNIR) and different LIBS plasma at 1 atm; lichen/biofilm coatings on Earth rocks.

experiments.name: Instrument field tests: GPR and drilling
also_account_for: Drilling in vacuum: no air cooling or flushing of cuttings; ice cuttings sublimate.
Cryogenic ice-regolith is much harder than Earth permafrost.
Earth subsurface moisture and salts dominate GPR attenuation.

experiments.name: Planetary protection, contamination blanks, life-detection false positives
also_account_for: No Earth surface is sterile; every blank still carries microbes and organics.
Stations and camps raise local contamination.
COSPAR policy for lunar polar / PSR missions asks for an organic-materials inventory (check the current category definitions).

experiments.name: Cave / pit robotics (skylight descent, mapping, comms)
also_account_for: Lunar pits/tubes may be far larger than terrestrial tubes.
Diviner-based studies estimate the shaded Tranquillitatis pit floor stays near ~290 K (verify before quoting).
Underground: no comms or GNSS; skylight descent by tether.
Earth caves are humid, biologically active and shaped by water.

experiments.name: Astronaut field-geology & EVA training
also_account_for: Suit dexterity, EVA time limits and 1/6 g gait are not reproduced.
Low sun and black shadows at the pole change what can be seen.
Earth outcrops are weathered and often vegetated.
